ledger.claim: POL-NS-01 limb (b) fails on the driver's own trace. EV-GPS-09104 places every one of the driver's 37 fixes at 559.3707 m from the pickup pin — min_distance_m, mean_distance_m and max_distance_m are identical — and the derived arrival block reports qualifying_fix_count 0, meaning not a single fix fell inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius that POL-NS-02 takes from fee_schedule.arrival_radius_m. The driver was never inside the pickup geofence at or before his 07:25:20 'arrived' event, so the conjunctive test in POL-NS-01 is broken and the SGD 4.00 fee is not chargeable.

POL-NS-01 limb (c) fails independently, so breaking (b) is not even necessary. The longest continuous in-geofence run in the trace is 0.0 seconds (longest_qualifying_run.duration_sec, fix_count 0), against the 300 second minimum for the STANDARD zone class, a measured shortfall of 300 seconds. Limb (c) measures the dwell from the first qualifying in-geofence fix, not from the 'arrived' tap, and no qualifying fix ever occurred — so the marker never ripened into a chargeable no-show.

Under POL-NS-02 the trace contains no qualifying in-radius fix at any point in the 15 minutes preceding the 07:31:00 driver cancellation, so the driver is not deemed to have arrived, POL-NS-01 limb (b) fails, and the rider is entitled to a full refund of the cancellation fee. EV-FARE-09104 itemises that fee at SGD 4.00 with payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00, so the sum to be returned to the filing rider is SGD 4.00.

POL-NS-05 applies squarely on the arrival marker itself. At the 07:25:20 'arrived' timestamp the trace puts the driver 559.3707 m from the pin — far beyond the clause's 300 m threshold — so the marker is FALSE and does not start the waiting clock. Recomputing the clock from the first qualifying in-geofence fix yields none (qualifying_fix_count 0), which is POL-NS-05(ii): the fee is refunded in full, no driver compensation is payable, and the trip must be recorded as a false-arrival event against the driver in the ruling's referrals list. The driver's own statement that he 'marked arrival and waited' is contradicted by his own trace.

POL-NS-06 makes the refund unconditional on this record. The effective in-geofence dwell is 0.0 seconds against the 300 second STANDARD minimum — a 300 second shortfall — so the cancellation fee 'is not chargeable and is refunded to the rider in full, whether or not the rider was present and whether or not the rider responded to messages.' Any suggestion that the state of the rider's own device excuses the charge is foreclosed by the clause's express terms; the waiting period is the consideration the fee was taken for.

POL-NS-03 cannot rescue the fee either, and the driver cannot convert this into a wrong-entrance case. The clause's entire test is that the driver held position 'not more than 400 m from the pickup pin'; here the driver's stationary fixes sit at 559.3707 m (min = mean = max), outside the 400 m ceiling. The wrong-entrance route — and with it any pin-ambiguity goodwill payment under POL-NS-03(ii) — is unavailable, and the refund stands at full.

POL-NS-06(i) is unavailable to the driver on the face of the trace: the derived accumulation block records run_count 0 and accumulated_sec 0.0, so there are no separate in-geofence intervals to sum in the first place. The waiting window also carries no advisory at all — EV-ADVIS-09104-01 is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and issue MISSING_ARTIFACT, and a MISSING advisory cannot meet the limb's 'present and populated' requirement. I disclose that artifact's impairment expressly. Nothing on this record repairs the 300 second shortfall.

No POL-NS-09 escalation trigger is met, so the case should be decided on its merits rather than held: the apparent tension between the driver's self-reported marker and the GPS is not an unresolved contradiction, because POL-NS-05 and POL-NS-02 resolve it on the clauses' own terms. The citable profile counters are clean — rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 0, below the 3 that POL-NS-09(d) requires, and both rider_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d and driver_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d are 0, so POL-NS-09(c) does not fire. Every artifact relied on above is COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0, so the confidence floor is not engaged and the money can move now.

The amount is not in dispute on the arithmetic, and the rider gains nothing there: SGD 4.00 is exactly what the fee schedule produces for this trip. The STANDARD zone-class fee is SGD 4.00 and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee is SGD 4.00; the resolution rule takes the GREATER of the two, which is the SGD 4.00 cancellation_fee line, and the fare breakdown's total_charged of SGD 4.00 reconciles with it. There is no POL-NS-08(d) fare defect for the rider to exploit, so if any clause makes the fee chargeable, the amount is already right.

On the trip record's own facts, two of POL-NS-01's four limbs hold. Limb (a): the record carries a driver 'arrived' event at 2026-09-04T07:25:20+08:00. Limb (d): the record shows no boarding (started_at is null) and the trip is terminated by the driver at 07:31:00 with cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW, one of the three codes the limb recognises, which is 5 minutes 40 seconds after the marker and therefore at or after a STANDARD 300-second dwell on that timeline. The dispute consequently turns entirely on the two GPS-derived limbs, (b) and (c).

The rider's exonerating route under POL-NS-04 cannot run on this record. Limb (a) fails at the threshold, because the chat log contains no rider message at all: its only two messages are the system arrival notice at 07:25:21 and the driver's own 'I have marked arrival.' at 07:25:40. Limb (c) is independently unsatisfied: the rider track's 17 fixes sit a uniform 519.46 m from the registered pickup pin VEN-BP-180 at a constant reported speed of 0.0, with rider_qualifying_fix_count of 0, far outside the 100 m STANDARD rider-presence radius the limb requires for the majority of qualifying fixes.

I do not stretch the decisive GPS point, I concede it. The driver's own trace places him a uniform 559.37 m from the pickup pin on every one of its 37 fixes, stationary at a reported speed of 0.0, with qualifying_fix_count of 0 and a longest qualifying in-geofence run of 0 seconds. That is more than half a kilometre outside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius and beyond even the 400 m wrong-entrance ceiling in POL-NS-03, so POL-NS-01 limbs (b) and (c) fail on this record, and no POL-NS-06 accumulation is open to rescue the dwell: EV-ADVIS-09104-01 is MISSING (issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight 0.0), so there is no traffic advisory covering this pickup road and no second in-geofence interval to add. On the GPS record alone the fee is not chargeable.

The one question this record does not settle by itself is which of the platform's two accounts of the arrival is authoritative, and that is the POL-NS-09(b) question. EV-TRIP-09104 records the driver 'arrived' at 07:25:20 with a wait_time_min of 5.7, and the platform broadcast that same assertion to the rider as the system message 'Your driver has arrived' at 07:25:21 in EV-CHAT-09104; EV-GPS-09104 places the driver 559.37 m from the pin throughout the same interval, with a longest qualifying run of 0 seconds. Both artifacts are admissible at weight 1.0, neither is impaired under POL-NS-08(a) to (d), and the driver's position is carried by the trace alone, with no per-fix horizontal accuracy in the bundle against which the 25 m filter can be checked independently. POL-NS-05 tells the Judge what follows if the trace is taken as authoritative on position, but it presumes the very point in issue. If the Judge treats the conflict as unresolved, the disputed SGD 4.00 should be HELD under POL-NS-09 rather than refunded while the reviewer settles which record is right; an escalated fee is held, not returned.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties. The SGD 4.00 no-show cancellation fee charged on trip TRP-09104 is refunded in full to the rider. The fee can stand only if all four conditions of POL-NS-01 hold, and two of them fail on the platform's own measurements. EV-GPS-09104 places the driver's vehicle 559.37 m from the registered pickup pin VEN-BP-180 on every one of its 37 fixes (min_distance_m = mean_distance_m = max_distance_m), with qualifying_fix_count 0 and a longest continuous in-geofence run of 0.0 seconds. The driver was therefore never inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival geofence at or before the 07:25:20 'arrived' event — limb (b) fails — and never accumulated any of the 300-second minimum dwell — limb (c) fails. The trip record's own 'arrived' event and 5.7-minute wait figure cannot repair that: under POL-NS-05 a marker set while the trace puts the driver more than 300 m from the pin is FALSE and does not start the waiting clock, which is recomputed from the first qualifying in-geofence fix; there was none. Because no qualifying in-geofence fix exists anywhere in the trip, POL-NS-05(ii) applies directly: full refund, no driver compensation, and the trip recorded as a false-arrival event — that last is the referral above. The same result follows independently under POL-NS-02 (no qualifying in-radius fix → the driver never arrived) and POL-NS-06 (0-second dwell against a 300-second minimum → the fee is refunded whether or not the rider was present or responded). The driver's argument that the gap between the trip record and the GPS must be escalated under POL-NS-09(b) is rejected: that trigger requires that no clause resolves the conflict, and POL-NS-05 is exactly the clause that resolves it. The remaining POL-NS-09 triggers were checked and do not fire — the confidence floor is not engaged, the citable counters are clean (rider no_show_disputes_30d 0; disputes_with_counterparty_90d 0 on both profiles), and the POL-NS-07 anti-farming test on the driver's trailing-30-day figures (1 termination against 120 completed trips) is nowhere near its thresholds, so no compensation is in issue. On the money itself there is no fare defect: the SGD 4.00 line equals the GREATER of the STANDARD zone-class fee (SGD 4.00) and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee (SGD 4.00), so POL-NS-08(d) is satisfied and the whole contested amount is what is refunded. The wrong-entrance route in POL-NS-03 cannot rescue the charge — it is confined to a driver stationary within 400 m of the pin, and this driver was at 559.37 m — so no pin-ambiguity goodwill arises. The rider's own track (519.46 m from the pin) and the absence of any rider chat message mean POL-NS-04 cannot be run, but that is immaterial, because the refund under POL-NS-05(ii)/POL-NS-02/POL-NS-06 does not depend on where the rider was. Finally, traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-09104-01 is MISSING (weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT); it carries no fact and forecloses any dwell accumulation under POL-NS-06(i), but it does not affect the refund. Neither party's profile was used as a ground of decision.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
referrals: POL-NS-05(ii): record trip TRP-09104 as a FALSE-ARRIVAL event against driver DRV-09104 — the 'arrived' marker was set at 2026-09-04T07:25:20+08:00 while EV-GPS-09104 placed the vehicle 559.37 m from the pickup pin, and no qualifying in-geofence fix exists anywhere in the trip.
